publications.name: Fast-Rotating Panoramic HDR Reconstruction from Single-Second Spikes
publications.summary: Problem: capturing panoramic HDR images during fast rotation is challenging due to motion blur and overexposure. Solution: proposed a side-by-side hybrid camera system requiring no spatial or temporal alignment; designed a spike-based panoramic reconstruction method and a colorization module based on a fine-tuned multimodal large language model; built a comprehensive dataset with synthetic and real-world spikes for HDR panoramic reconstruction and colorization. Result: reconstructed full-color panoramic HDR images from one-second spike acquisition under fast-rotation conditions.

publications.name: Seam-Guided Unsupervised Image Stitching with Parallax-Aware Mask Generation
publications.publisher: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (CCF-B)
publications.summary: Problem: image stitching under large parallax is challenging due to the conflict between content alignment and shape preservation, while spatially varying transformations often cause unexpected distortions. Solution: designed an edge-enhanced mask generation module to distinguish large-parallax regions and suppress excessive distortions; proposed a seam-guided alignment strategy that iteratively refines local registration for improved stitching consistency; built a new parallax dataset to improve generalization. Result: effectively removes misaligned regions while maintaining shape consistency, especially in challenging parallax scenarios.

work.name: Baidu Online Network Technology Co., Ltd.
work.summary: Conducted algorithm research on image understanding and image editing generation.
highlights: Project 1 — Large Multimodal Models for Image Understanding and Intelligent Portrait Retouching Parameter Prediction.
Problem: intelligent portrait retouching requires a vision-language model to perceive facial flaws and predict structured retouching parameters, replacing inefficient manual tuning.
Solution: fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B with LoRA for multi-label retouching parameter prediction, with face images as input and structured JSON retouching functions and levels as output.
Stage 1 (SFT): trained on Gemini-labeled instruction data for visual perception and parameter prediction.

Stage 2 (Paired-data SFT): built a data flywheel by using the Stage-1 model to infer parameters on 160K images and applying AI retouching tools to generate before-after pairs as augmented training data.
Result: improved prediction F1-score from 81% to 86% on a 900-image test set.
Project 2 — Creative Image Generation and AI ID-Photo Outfit Replacement.
Problem: AI ID-photo outfit replacement can fail when the subject's head and neck are misaligned or the neck region is missing, producing unnatural results.
Preprocessing: extracted human keypoints to align the head and neck before generation.
Stage 1 (Data Construction): used Nano Banana 2 to construct head-neck images, applied SAM3 for neck segmentation, and simulated structural missing regions via random masking to build training data.
Stage 2 (Neck Inpainting): fine-tuned Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 to regenerate missing neck structures and complete portraits from incomplete inputs.
Stage 3 (Post-processing): applied texture phase-shift overlay to mitigate skin over-smoothing and used keypoints to place clothing.
Result: achieved natural AI ID-photo outfit replacement with correct neck structure and realistic skin texture.

projects.name: Spherical-Projection Panoramic Image Stitching System for Data Centers
projects.summary: Developed a fast spherical-projection panoramic stitching system for data-center scenarios.
highlights: Problem: a single camera has limited field of view in data-center scenes, requiring panoramic reconstruction from multiple views.

Solution: proposed a fast spherical-projection panoramic stitching algorithm, corrected lens distortion, estimated focal length via cylindrical projection, and built a spherical projection model to fuse 30 images into an equirectangular projection panorama supporting 3D viewing.
Result: reconstructs a full panorama in one second and was deployed in China Tower's production business.
Authored one patent related to the project, owned by China Tower.

references.name: Research Statement
references.reference: My research lies at the intersection of geometric computer vision and generative image modeling. Through my stitching work (TCSVT) and panoramic reconstruction (ACM MM), I identified large parallax as a fundamental limitation of alignment-based methods, and I am interested in exploring image editing models for local parallax region regeneration. During my internship, I observed shared texture fidelity challenges across tasks: VAE decoders losing high-frequency detail in ID-photo generation, tiling artifacts in repetitive textures such as grass, and the inability of super-resolution models to recover semantic information. These observations motivate my PhD research interest: understanding and solving texture-faithful generative editing under geometric constraints.
